how.title: Three steps. No accounts required.
how.intro: shhnote encrypts your secret in the browser before anything touches the network. The encryption key lives in the URL fragment — a part of the URL that browsers never send to servers.

steps.title: Encrypt
steps.body: Your secret is encrypted on your own device before anything is sent. The key to unlock it is never uploaded.

steps.title: Share
steps.body: It lives in the part of the link after the # — which browsers keep local and never send to a server.

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.body: The recipient's browser unlocks it locally. A one-time secret is deleted from the server the moment it is opened; a timed one when it expires. Even we can't recover it.

hood.title: The cryptography, spelled out.
hood.intro: No hand-waving. Here's exactly what protects your secret, and where each piece runs — so you can verify the claims instead of taking them on faith.

specs.label: Encryption
specs.body: Authenticated symmetric encryption. Every secret is sealed with a 256-bit key and an integrity tag, so tampering is detected — not just left unreadable.

specs.label: Key derivation
specs.body: Optional passphrases are stretched with a memory-hard KDF, making offline brute-force attacks slow and costly even on purpose-built hardware.

specs.label: Randomness
specs.body: Keys and nonces are drawn from the browser's cryptographically secure generator. Never Math.random(), never predictable.

specs.label: Key custody
specs.body: The decryption key rides after the # in your link. Browsers never transmit the fragment, so the key that unlocks the secret never reaches our servers.

specs.label: In transit
specs.body: Only ciphertext ever leaves your device, carried over modern TLS. What we receive is an opaque blob we have no way to open.

specs.label: At rest
specs.body: We persist the encrypted blob, one-way hashes of the values used to find or burn it, its lifetime and a rounded expiry — nothing else. No plaintext, no keys, no sender or recipient metadata.

items.label: DevOps & Engineering
items.title: Credentials & Keys
items.body: Stop pasting API keys, database passwords, and SSH keys into chat threads. Share them as one-time links that self-destruct after use. Integrate with CI/CD pipelines via the API.

items.label: Privacy-conscious users
items.title: Share without a trace
items.body: Works in Tor Browser at the Safer level. No CAPTCHAs, no browser fingerprinting, no external requests. Every font and asset is self-hosted.

items.label: IT & Onboarding
items.title: Provision access securely
items.body: Send new hires initial credentials, VPN configs, or Wi-Fi passwords without leaving traces in email threads or ticketing systems. Script it through the API for batch onboarding.

items.label: Legal & Regulatory
items.title: Compliance-sensitive records
items.body: Send a patient record, case file, or financial statement to a client or colleague without it sitting in an inbox that's subject to discovery, audit, or breach disclosure.

items.label: Personal
items.title: Everyday secrets
items.body: Send your accountant tax document passwords. Share streaming credentials with family. Give a contractor your alarm code. Send sensitive files securely. Simple enough for anyone.

items.label: Misc
items.title: Gift codes or surprise reveals
items.body: Send a gift card code, a surprise, scavenger/treasure hunt clue, or a reveal that vanishes after they've seen it.

cta.title: Stop sharing sensitive info in plaintext
cta.intro: Create a one-time encrypted link in seconds. Or create a multi-view encrypted link that expires in a few hours or days. Add extra protection with a password. No account needed. Nothing that identifies you is kept.

secret.title: Someone shared a secret with you

armed.title: Someone shared a secret with you
armed.intro: It's decrypted in your browser. If it was sent as a single view, it's deleted the moment you open it — so reveal it only when you're ready to read and save it.
armed.noscript: JavaScript is needed to decrypt this secret in your browser. Please turn it on to view the secret.
armed.passphraseNote: If the sender set a passphrase, you'll be asked for it after you press the button.
armed.callout: Nothing has been fetched yet — this is all an automated scanner sees. We keep the reveal manual on purpose, so email security, chat previews and antivirus can't open your secret before you do.

working.title: Decrypting in your browser…
working.intro: Fetching the ciphertext and unlocking it locally with the key from your link. It never leaves this tab in readable form.

passphrase.title: This secret needs a passphrase
passphrase.intro: The sender added a second lock. Retries happen in your browser; nothing is sent to the server.
passphrase.label: Passphrase
passphrase.wrong: That passphrase didn't work. Try again.

revealed.singleView: Destroyed · this was the only view
revealed.title: Here it is. Save what you need now.
revealed.intro: This secret was decrypted in your browser. Refresh this page and it's gone from here.
revealed.closeWarning: Handle it carefully — once you close this tab there's no way to retrieve it again, from you or from us.

notFound.title: No secret found here.
notFound.intro: This link is invalid, or the secret it pointed to has already been viewed, expired, or been destroyed. For your privacy, this site keeps no record of which — nothing about a secret's history is ever stored.
notFound.callout: If you still need the secret, ask the sender to create a fresh link — and double-check you copied the whole URL, including the part after the #.

errors.network: Couldn't reach the server. Try again in a moment.
errors.corrupt: This secret couldn't be decrypted. The link may be incomplete.
errors.wasm: This passphrase needs WebAssembly, which your browser or its security level has switched off (Tor Browser at "Safer", for example). Allow it and try again.

armed.title: Destroy this secret?
armed.intro: This is a burn link. Nothing has happened yet. Confirming deletes the encrypted secret and its file(s) permanently — before anyone else can open them.
armed.noscript: This page needs JavaScript to do anything. Please turn it on.

done.title: This secret has been destroyed.
done.intro: You just used the burn link. The encrypted secret and its file(s) have been permanently erased from our servers — before anyone else could open them.
done.callout: Anyone who opens the original share link from here on will simply be told no secret was found — with no way to tell whether it was viewed, expired, or burned. Nothing about it is kept.

notFound.title: Nothing to destroy.
notFound.intro: This burn link is invalid, or the secret was already viewed, expired, or destroyed.

armed.title: Report a secret link
armed.intro: Paste a link you believe shares something it shouldn't. If the secret is still active it is removed immediately. We can't see what it contains, so there is nothing to review and nothing to tell you.
armed.noscript: This page needs JavaScript to do anything. Please turn it on.
armed.label: Secret link
armed.help: The full link including the part after the #. It is used only to find the secret; it is not stored.
armed.invalid: That doesn't look like a secret link from this site.

done.title: Thanks, that's handled.
done.intro: If that link pointed at an active secret, it is gone now. We keep a record that a report was received, nothing more.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.heading: This page doesn't exist.
notFound.intro: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved or been removed.
notFound.callout: Following a secret link? It ends in /s# and a long code. Check that it was copied in full, including everything after the #. Nothing was opened here.
